hooks.text: A spacecraft designed to die in thirty-two minutes lasted two hours.
A lander built for thirty-two minutes survived two hours on Venus.
A Soviet probe survived the solar system's most crushing world.

title: The Soviet Lander That Defied Death on Venus
description: The Soviet Venera 13 lander was designed to survive 32 minutes on Venus but lasted over two hours, capturing the first color photos of another world.

beats.text: A spacecraft designed to die in thirty-two minutes lasted two hours.
On March 1, 1982, the Soviet Union's Venera 13 lander plunged into the atmosphere of Venus.
beats.visual: artist's concept of the Venera 13 probe descending through Venus clouds, 1982

beats.text: It faced ninety atmospheres of pressure and temperatures near four hundred sixty degrees Celsius.
beats.visual: global view of Venus atmosphere clouds, Mariner 10, 1974

beats.text: The probe drilled for soil samples and captured the first color photographs ever taken on another planet.
beats.visual: first color panorama photograph of the Venusian surface from Venera 13, 1982

beats.text: These images showed a jagged orange landscape littered with rocks and discarded lens caps.
beats.visual: Venera 13 surface photograph highlighting the landing site rocks, 1982

beats.text: Years later, a scientist claimed the photos showed a moving alien shaped like a scorpion.
beats.visual: Venera 13 photograph showing the landing site rocks, 1982

beats.text: Experts proved the alien was actually a lens cap that fell off during landing.
beats.visual: Venera 13 surface photograph highlighting the discarded camera lens cap, 1982

beats.text: Soviet engineers celebrated this machine, which was much more than just a spacecraft designed to die in thirty-two minutes.
beats.visual: Soviet engineers inspecting a Venera spacecraft model in a cleanroom, 1981
